newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: UKIO REGRETS HOIUPANK TALKS CAME TO NOTHING.
newsitem.headline: UKIO REGRETS HOIUPANK TALKS CAME TO NOTHING.

text.p: Lithuania's Ukio Bank said on Thursday that it had been in talks with Estonia's Hoiupank for a few months and regretted it led to no result.
Hoiupank earlier announced that it was abandoning plans for the timebeing to expand into Lithuania and would instead concentrate on Russia and Ukraine.

"The negotiations with Hoiupank lasted for a few months and gave no results. We slightly regret it since the potential partner was reliable and respectable," Ukio Bank chairman Raimondas Rapkevichius told Reuters.
"We were talking on possible co-operation in leasing, commercial banking and credit cards," Rapkevichius added.
The two banks also discussed the possibility to move to the Ukrainian market together, Rapkevichius said.

"Lithuania's banking sector is now rather competetive and I understand Hoiupank's decision to move to the Ukrainian market where the same amount of investment will give higher returns," Rapkevichius said
"As far as I know, Hoiupank also held talks with the Lithuanian Agricultural Bank and Litimpeks," he said.
Hoiupank said its plans in Lithuania were not ruled out in the long term.
